symbols.name: \(\mathcal Y\)
symbols.def: The state space of the observed and potential outcomes.

symbols.name: \(a\)
symbols.def: The treatment arm whose counterfactual law is studied.

symbols.name: \(A\)
symbols.def: The observed treatment variable.

symbols.name: \(Y(0),Y(1)\)
symbols.def: The two potential outcomes under the binary treatment interventions.

symbols.name: \(Y\)
symbols.def: The realized outcome.

symbols.name: \(e\)
symbols.def: The scalar probability \(e=\Pr(A=a)\) in the fixed covariate stratum.

symbols.name: \(P\)
symbols.def: The law \(P=\mathcal L(Y\mid A=a)\).

symbols.name: \(Q\)
symbols.def: A candidate for \(\mathcal L(Y(a))=P(Y\in\cdot\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a))\).

symbols.name: \(R\)
symbols.def: The residual law representing \(\mathcal L(Y(a)\mid A\ne a)\).

symbols.name: \(c\)
symbols.def: The propensity-induced cap \(c=1/e\).

symbols.name: \(f\)
symbols.space: finite continuous convex functions \(f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\) with \(f(1)=0\)
symbols.def: The generator shared by the one-sided and mutual-absolute-continuity Jung--Kang divergence ambiguity classes.

symbols.name: \(f_{\mathrm{KL}}\)
symbols.def: The generator \(f_{\mathrm{KL}}(t)=t\log t\), with \(0\log 0=0\).

symbols.name: \(f_c\)
symbols.def: The cap hinge \(f_c(t)=(t-c)_+\).

symbols.name: \(D_f(P\|Q)\)
symbols.def: \(D_f(P\|Q)=\int_{\mathcal Y}f(dP/dQ)\,dQ\) when \(P\ll Q\).

symbols.name: \(\mathfrak M_e(P)\)
symbols.def: The Assumption-4 class defined in \(\mathrm{def:bow\text{-}compatible}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathfrak L_e(P)\)
symbols.def: The \(R\ll P\) mixture class defined in \(\mathrm{def:mixture\text{-}class}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)\)
symbols.def: The positive-density ball defined in \(\mathrm{def:jk\text{-}ball}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathfrak H_c\)
symbols.space: class of finite continuous convex generators
symbols.def: The affine-equivalence class defined in \(\mathrm{def:hinge\text{-}class}\).

symbols.name: \(p\)
symbols.def: The scalar \(p=P(B)\) for a measurable event \(B\subseteq\mathcal Y\).

symbols.name: \(q_0\)
symbols.def: The boundary coordinate \(q_0=ep\) for a full-support binary observational law.

symbols.name: \(\varepsilon\)
symbols.def: A positive perturbation for the binary candidate probability \(q=ep-\varepsilon\).

symbols.name: \(q\)
symbols.def: The success probability in the binary candidate law \(Q=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q)\).

symbols.name: \(y\)
symbols.def: A generic threshold indexing the counterfactual CDF.

symbols.name: \(L_e(p),U_e(p)\)
symbols.def: The atom-aware piecewise maps defined in \(\mathrm{def:cdf\text{-}maps}\).

symbols.name: \(h\)
symbols.def: A measurable bounded function whose counterfactual expectation is bounded.

symbols.name: \(\underline\theta_h,\overline\theta_h\)
symbols.def: The infimum and supremum of \(E_Q[h]\) over \(Q\in\mathfrak M_e(P)\).

symbols.name: \(\mathfrak B^{\mathrm{law}}_{f,e}(P)\)
symbols.def: The P-supported intersection defined in \(\mathrm{def:lawful\text{-}correction}\).
symbols.role: exact generic feasible-set intersection on an alphabet restricted to \(\operatorname{supp}(P)\)

symbols.name: \(\mathcal O_f\)
symbols.def: The stable ball-feasible but SCM-illegal region delivered by \(\mathrm{thm:open\text{-}illegal\text{-}dichotomy}\).

symbols.name: \(n\)
symbols.def: The number of independent observational units.

symbols.name: \(\alpha\)
symbols.def: The target familywise error probability.

symbols.name: \(\widehat e_n,\widehat F_{P,n}\)
symbols.def: \(\widehat e_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}\) and \(\widehat F_{P,n}(y)=n_a^{-1}\sum_{i:A_i=a}\mathbf 1\{Y_i\le y\}\) when \(n_a>0\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}\)

symbols.name: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{dir}}\)

symbols.name: \(\mathfrak M^{\to}_e(P)\)
symbols.def: The class defined in \(\mathrm{def:bow\text{-}compatible\text{-}one\text{-}sided}\), without the mutual-absolute-continuity member property.

symbols.name: \(\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)\)

symbols.name: \(\mathfrak B^{\to}_{f,e}(P)\)
symbols.def: The ball defined in \(\mathrm{def:jk\text{-}ball\text{-}one\text{-}sided}\), requiring only \(P\ll Q\).

symbols.name: \(L^{\to}_e(p),U^{\to}_e(p)\)
symbols.def: The continuous maps defined in \(\mathrm{def:cdf\text{-}maps\text{-}one\text{-}sided}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathfrak B^{\mathrm{law},\to}_{f,e}(P)\)
symbols.def: The intersection defined in \(\mathrm{def:lawful\text{-}correction\text{-}one\text{-}sided}\).
symbols.role: exact generic feasible-set intersection on an alphabet that may retain cells outside \(\operatorname{supp}(P)\)

symbols.name: \(e_1,e_2\)
symbols.def: Two distinct propensity values used to state the heterogeneous-propensity impossibility.

symbols.name: \(f_e\)
symbols.def: The adaptive hinge \(f_e(t)=(t-1/e)_+\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal X\)

symbols.name: \(X\)
symbols.def: The observed pretreatment covariate.

symbols.name: \(\kappa\)

symbols.space: set of pairs of Markov kernels from \(\mathcal X\) to \(\mathcal Y\)

assumptions.condition: The observed vertices \(A,Y\) have the bow ADMG \(A\to Y\) and \(A\leftrightarrow Y\), represented by a nonparametric latent-variable SCM.

standard.name: Nonparametric SCM Markov to a bow ADMG

assumptions.condition: The realized outcome satisfies \(Y=Y(A)\) almost surely.
Every candidate bow SCM satisfies \(\mathcal L(Y(a)\mid A=a)\sim\mathcal L(Y(a))\).

standard.name: Mutual absolute continuity of observational and interventional arm laws

assumptions.condition: The observations \((A_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^n\) are independent and identically distributed draws from the observed bow-SCM law.

One global nonparametric latent-variable SCM has observed vertices \(X,A,Y\), observed arrows \(X\to A\), \(X\to Y\), and \(A\to Y\), and a latent variable \(U\) that may be a parent of each of \(X,A,Y\).

There is a constant \(0<\kappa\le1/2\) and a measurable propensity system \(\boldsymbol e=(e_0,e_1)\) on \(\mathcal X\) such that \(e_a(x)\in[\kappa,1-\kappa]\) and \(e_0(x)+e_1(x)=1\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\).
The global SCM satisfies \(Y=Y(A)\) almost surely.
For both arms on one common measurable \(\mu_X\)-conull set, the conditional interventional kernel is absolutely continuous with respect to the observed arm kernel: \(Q_a(x,\cdot)\ll P_a(x,\cdot)\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak M_e(P)\)
definitions.construction: For \(0<e<1\), \(\mathfrak M_e(P)=\{Q\in\mathcal P(\mathcal Y): Q=\mathcal L(Y(a))\text{ in a bow-ADMG SCM with }\Pr(A=a)=e,\ \mathcal L(Y\mid A=a)=P,\text{ and member properties }\mathrm{ass:bow\text{-}structure},\mathrm{ass:consistency},\mathrm{ass:positivity},\mathrm{ass:mutual\text{-}ac}\}\). At the boundary, define \(\mathfrak M_1(P)=\{P\}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak L_e(P)\)
definitions.construction: For \(0<e\le1\), \(\mathfrak L_e(P)=\{Q\in\mathcal P(\mathcal Y): Q=eP+(1-e)R\text{ for some }R\in\mathcal P(\mathcal Y)\text{ with }R\ll P\}\); hence \(\mathfrak L_1(P)=\{P\}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak H_c\)
definitions.construction: \(\{f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R: f\text{ is finite, continuous, convex, }f(1)=0,\text{ and there exists }b\in\mathbb R\text{ such that }g_b(t)=f(t)-b(t-1)\text{ obeys }g_b(t)=0\text{ for }0\le t\le c\text{ and }g_b(t)>0\text{ for }t>c\}\).

definitions.name: \(L_e,U_e\)
definitions.construction: For \(0\le e\le1\), \(L_e(p)=e p\) for \(0\le p<1\), \(L_e(1)=1\), \(U_e(0)=0\), and \(U_e(p)=e p+1-e\) for \(0<p\le1\). In particular, \(L_1(p)=U_1(p)=p\) for every \(p\in[0,1]\).

definitions.name: \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}\)
definitions.construction: Let \(n_a=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}\), \(\delta_e=\sqrt{\log(4/\alpha)/(2n)}\), and \(\delta_F=\sqrt{\log(4/\alpha)/(2n_a)}\) when \(n_a>0\). Form \(I_e=[\widehat e_n-\delta_e,\widehat e_n+\delta_e]\cap[0,1]\) and \(I_F(y)=[\widehat F_{P,n}(y)-\delta_F,\widehat F_{P,n}(y)+\delta_F]\cap[0,1]\). For every \(y\), \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}(y)\) is the coordinatewise rectangular hull of \(\{(L_\eta(p),U_\eta(p)):\eta\in I_e,\ p\in I_F(y)\}\); when \(n_a=0\), set it to \([0,1]^2\).

definitions.name: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{dir}}\)
definitions.construction: Handle: linearize the joint pre-endpoint empirical process \((\widehat e_n,\widehat F_{P,n})\), derive the Hadamard directional derivative of the piecewise map \((e,F_P)\mapsto(L_e\circ F_P,U_e\circ F_P)\), and estimate that derivative inside a Fang--Santos multiplier or numerical-delta bootstrap before taking the supremum over thresholds and arms.

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak M^{\to}_e(P)\)
definitions.construction: For \(0<e<1\), \(\mathfrak M^{\to}_e(P)\) is the set of laws \(Q=\mathcal L(Y(a))\) realized in a nonparametric latent-variable bow-ADMG SCM with \(\Pr(A=a)=e\), \(\mathcal L(Y\mid A=a)=P\), and member properties \(\mathrm{ass:bow\text{-}structure}\), \(\mathrm{ass:consistency}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:positivity}\), without imposing \(\mathrm{ass:mutual\text{-}ac}\). At the boundary define \(\mathfrak M^{\to}_1(P)=\{P\}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)\)
definitions.construction: For \(0<e\le1\), \(\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)=\{Q\in\mathcal P(\mathcal Y):Q=eP+(1-e)R\text{ for some }R\in\mathcal P(\mathcal Y)\}\); hence \(\mathfrak L^{\to}_1(P)=\{P\}\).

definitions.name: \(L^{\to}_e,U^{\to}_e\)
definitions.construction: For \(0\le e\le1\) and \(0\le p\le1\), define \(L^{\to}_e(p)=ep\) and \(U^{\to}_e(p)=ep+1-e\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak M^{\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)\)
definitions.construction: Let \(\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\) be standard Borel spaces, let \(\mu_X\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X)\), let \(0<\kappa\le1/2\), let \(\boldsymbol e=(e_0,e_1)\) satisfy \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}overlap}\), and let \(\boldsymbol P=(P_0,P_1)\) be Markov kernels from \(\mathcal X\) to \(\mathcal Y\).  Then \(\mathfrak M^{\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)\) is the set of pairs \(\boldsymbol Q=(Q_0,Q_1)\) of Markov kernels for which one SCM satisfying \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}bow\text{-}architecture}\), \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}overlap}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}consistency}\) has \(X\sim\mu_X\) and admits one measurable \(\mu_X\)-conull set \(S\) on which, simultaneously for \(a=0,1\), \(\Pr(A=a\mid X=x)=e_a(x)\), \(\mathcal L(Y\mid A=a,X=x)=P_a(x,\cdot)\), and \(\mathcal L(Y(a)\mid X=x)=Q_a(x,\cdot)\).  Conditional kernels are versions and no restriction is placed on \(S^c\).  No reverse-support condition is imposed.

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak L^{\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)\)
definitions.construction:
Under the same self-contained setup of standard Borel \(\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\), \(\mu_X\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X)\), \(0<\kappa\le1/2\), measurable \(\boldsymbol e=(e_0,e_1)\) satisfying \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}overlap}\), and Markov kernels \(\boldsymbol P=(P_0,P_1)\), the class \(\mathfrak L^{\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)\) consists of pairs \(\boldsymbol Q=(Q_0,Q_1)\) of Markov kernels for which there are Markov kernels \(\boldsymbol R=(R_0,R_1)\) and one measurable \(\mu_X\)-conull set \(S\) such that, for every \(x\in S\) and \(a=0,1\),
\[
 Q_a(x,\cdot)=e_a(x)P_a(x,\cdot)+(1-e_a(x))R_a(x,\cdot).
\]
No restriction is imposed on the versions over \(S^c\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak M_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)\)
definitions.construction: Let \(\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\) be standard Borel spaces, let \(\mu_X\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X)\), let \(0<\kappa\le1/2\), let measurable \(\boldsymbol e=(e_0,e_1)\) satisfy \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}overlap}\), and let \(\boldsymbol P=(P_0,P_1)\) be Markov kernels from \(\mathcal X\) to \(\mathcal Y\).  Then \(\mathfrak M_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)\) is the set of pairs \(\boldsymbol Q=(Q_0,Q_1)\) for which one SCM satisfying \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}bow\text{-}architecture}\), \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}overlap}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}consistency}\) has \(X\sim\mu_X\) and admits one measurable \(\mu_X\)-conull set \(S\) on which, simultaneously for \(a=0,1\), \(\Pr(A=a\mid X=x)=e_a(x)\), \(\mathcal L(Y\mid A=a,X=x)=P_a(x,\cdot)\), \(\mathcal L(Y(a)\mid X=x)=Q_a(x,\cdot)\), and \(Q_a(x,\cdot)\ll P_a(x,\cdot)\).  Conditional kernels are versions and no restriction is placed on \(S^c\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak L_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)\)
definitions.construction: Under the same self-contained setup of standard Borel \(\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\), \(\mu_X\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X)\), \(0<\kappa\le1/2\), measurable \(\boldsymbol e=(e_0,e_1)\) satisfying \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}overlap}\), and Markov kernels \(\boldsymbol P=(P_0,P_1)\), the class \(\mathfrak L_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)\) consists of pairs \(\boldsymbol Q=(Q_0,Q_1)\) for which there are Markov kernels \(\boldsymbol R=(R_0,R_1)\) and one measurable \(\mu_X\)-conull set \(S\) such that \(Q_a=e_aP_a+(1-e_a)R_a\) and \(R_a(x,\cdot)\ll P_a(x,\cdot)\) for both arms and every \(x\in S\).  No restriction is imposed on the versions over \(S^c\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak B^{\mathrm{ad},\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)\)
definitions.construction:
Let \(\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\) be standard Borel spaces, let \(\mu_X\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X)\), let \(0<\kappa\le1/2\), let measurable \(\boldsymbol e=(e_0,e_1)\) satisfy \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}overlap}\), and let \(\boldsymbol P=(P_0,P_1)\) be Markov kernels from \(\mathcal X\) to \(\mathcal Y\).  Define \(f_{a,x}(t)=(t-1/e_a(x))_+\).  The class \(\mathfrak B^{\mathrm{ad},\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)\) consists of pairs \(\boldsymbol Q=(Q_0,Q_1)\) of Markov kernels from \(\mathcal X\) to \(\mathcal Y\) for which there is one measurable \(\mu_X\)-conull set \(S\) such that, for every \(x\in S\) and \(a=0,1\), \(P_a(x,\cdot)\ll Q_a(x,\cdot)\) and
\[
 D_{f_{a,x}}(P_a(x,\cdot)\|Q_a(x,\cdot))\le B_{f_{a,x}}(e_a(x)).
\]
The constraints are fiberwise, not integrated over \(x\), and no assertion is made at a specified point in \(S^c\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak B^{\mathrm{ad}}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)\)
definitions.construction:
Let \(\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\) be standard Borel spaces, let \(\mu_X\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X)\), let \(0<\kappa\le1/2\), let measurable \(\boldsymbol e=(e_0,e_1)\) satisfy \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}overlap}\), and let \(\boldsymbol P=(P_0,P_1)\) be Markov kernels from \(\mathcal X\) to \(\mathcal Y\).  With \(f_{a,x}(t)=(t-1/e_a(x))_+\), the class \(\mathfrak B^{\mathrm{ad}}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)\) consists of pairs \(\boldsymbol Q=(Q_0,Q_1)\) of Markov kernels from \(\mathcal X\) to \(\mathcal Y\) for which there is one measurable \(\mu_X\)-conull set \(S\) such that, for every \(x\in S\) and \(a=0,1\), \(P_a(x,\cdot)\sim Q_a(x,\cdot)\) and
\[
 D_{f_{a,x}}(P_a(x,\cdot)\|Q_a(x,\cdot))\le B_{f_{a,x}}(e_a(x)).
\]
The constraints are fiberwise, not integrated over \(x\), and no assertion is made at a specified point in \(S^c\).

statements.statement: For every standard Borel \(\mathcal Y\), arm \(a\), probability law \(P\), and \(0<e<1\), the bow-ADMG compatible interventional laws are exactly the propensity mixtures: \(\mathfrak M_e(P)=\mathfrak L_e(P)\). Equivalently, \(Q\in\mathfrak M_e(P)\) if and only if \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\) for some \(R\ll P\), or if and only if \(Q\sim P\) and \(dP/dQ\le1/e\) \(Q\)-almost surely. Every admissible \(R\) is realized by a latent construction with \(U=(A,Y(0),Y(1))\).
statements.justification: This structural input identifies the exact compatible-SCM law set needed by the flagship generator frontier.
statements.gap: Jung and Kang (2026, Assumption 4; Theorem 5, equations (3)--(4); proof in Appendix E) prove that compatible interventional laws lie in the calibrated ambiguity class, while Huber contamination results do not prove realization by the specified bow SCM.
statements.consumer: It supplies the legal feasible set for every downstream distributional or expectation bound in \(\texttt{itbound}\).

statements.statement: Fix \(0<e<1\) and \(c=1/e\). For every finite continuous convex \(f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\) with \(f(1)=0\), the following are equivalent: \(\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)=\mathfrak L_e(P)\) for every probability law \(P\) on every standard Borel space; this equality holds for every full-support binary \(P\); and \(f\in\mathfrak H_c\). Thus, modulo the divergence-invariant affine term \(b(t-1)\), exactness holds if and only if the generator vanishes on \([0,1/e]\) and is strictly positive on \((1/e,\infty)\).
statements.justification: This is the flagship result: the affine-invariant iff identifies precisely which divergence ambiguity classes are causally complete rather than merely valid outer sets.
statements.gap: Fauss, Zoubir, and Poor (2018) preserve least-favorable tests under a constructed density band and ask when uncertainty sets themselves coincide; Jung and Kang (2026) do not characterize the generators giving set equality.
statements.consumer: Divergence designers obtain a complete rule for selecting a propensity-calibrated generator whose feasible laws are exactly the bow-SCM laws.

statements.statement: Fix \(0<e<1\), let \(c=1/e\), and suppose \(f\notin\mathfrak H_c\). There is a nonempty Euclidean-open set \(\mathcal O_f\subset(0,1)^2\) of binary pairs \((p,q)\), interpreted as \(P=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\) and \(Q=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q)\), such that \(Q\in\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)\setminus\mathfrak L_e(P)\) throughout \(\mathcal O_f\). More precisely, either no affine representative of \(f\) is affine on \([0,c]\), in which case \(\mathcal O_f\) can be chosen with \(D_f(P\|Q)<B_f(e)\), or an affine representative vanishes on \([0,c]\) and on \([0,d]\) for some \(d>c\), in which case an open illegal set is contained in the zero-divergence face. This dichotomy includes nondifferentiable and piecewise-linear generators.
statements.justification: This stable converse certifies that every failure of the flagship frontier persists under perturbation and is not a hand-tuned counterexample.
statements.gap: Sason and Verdu (2016) analyze hinge divergences and bounded likelihood ratios, while Guntuboyina, Saha, and Schiebinger (2014) reduce divergence extrema to small alphabets; neither proves this fully quantified open-set dichotomy for every finite convex generator.
statements.consumer: The result gives a robust legality diagnostic for KL, Hellinger, chi-square, total-variation, Jensen--Shannon, and every other failing generator.

statements.statement: Let \(\mathcal Y=\mathbb R\). For every threshold \(y\), write \(p=F_P(y)\). The exact bow-SCM identified interval is \(\{F_Q(y):Q\in\mathfrak M_e(P)\}=[L_e(p),U_e(p)]\). Each endpoint is attained by a bow-ADMG SCM satisfying all maintained support conditions, including when \(P\) has an atom at \(y\), \(p=0\), or \(p=1\). For \(0<p<1\), the witnesses choose residual laws supported on \(({-}\infty,y]\) or its complement; the boundary formulas force the unique value \(0\) or \(1\).
statements.justification: The interval has the familiar Manski/contamination form away from support contacts; the delivered contribution is the atom-aware mutual-AC boundary discontinuity and its attainment by bow-SCMs satisfying the maintained support condition.
statements.gap: Manski-style worst-case and contamination envelopes give the standard interior linear bounds, but do not certify the mutual-AC boundary values or bow-SCM attainment in the two support regimes.
statements.consumer: It supplies the exact CDF map appropriate to each support convention and the mutual map used for inference.

statements.statement: For every admissible generator \(f\), \(\mathfrak B^{\mathrm{law}}_{f,e}(P)=\mathfrak L_e(P)=\mathfrak M_e(P)\). For each \(h\in L^\infty(P)\), the exact mutual-AC support-function endpoints are \(\underline\theta_h=eE_P[h]+(1-e)\operatorname*{ess\,inf}_P h\) and \(\overline\theta_h=eE_P[h]+(1-e)\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_P h\). On a finite alphabet restricted to \(\operatorname{supp}(P)\), adding the cap constraints \(q_j\ge ep_j\) to a divergence program yields the exact mutual-AC class, weakly tightens every linear bounded-query optimization, and strictly tightens it whenever a unique relaxed optimizer violates the cap. For every \(f\notin\mathfrak H_c\), a bounded binary query has a strict legality gap on a nonempty open region of observational laws.
statements.justification: The theorem turns the cap into an exact feasible-set correction under either explicitly stated optimization ambient space.
statements.gap: The frozen evidence does not establish which support convention the itbound code uses, so the theorem gives both checkable branches instead of guessing.
statements.consumer: A source audit selects the correct branch before the itbound and IHDP re-analysis.

statements.statement: Under independent observational sampling, the band \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}\) satisfies \(\Pr\{(L_e(F_P(y)),U_e(F_P(y)))\in\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}(y)\text{ for every }y\in\mathbb R\}\ge1-\alpha\) for every \(n\), including \(n_a=0\), arbitrary atoms, and contact with \(F_P(y)\in\{0,1\}\). The guarantee follows by combining a propensity Hoeffding interval with a conditional Dvoretzky--Kiefer--Wolfowitz band and propagating their joint rectangle through the full piecewise endpoint map.
statements.justification: This inference layer propagates the lawful endpoint consequence with an honest finite-sample simultaneous guarantee at nonsmooth boundary cases.
statements.gap: Masten, Poirier, and Zhang (2024) develop uniform bands over a sensitivity index, and Jung and Kang (2026) give scalar orthogonal inference; neither covers the threshold-indexed lawful endpoint pair with boundary contacts.
statements.consumer: The IHDP audit can report simultaneous uncertainty for the complete corrected CDF envelope rather than pointwise error bars.

statements.statement: Can the handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{dir}}\) be used to construct a nonconservative asymptotic \(1-\alpha\) simultaneous band for both lawful endpoint processes, uniformly over a tie-inclusive local class that permits positive-mass atoms and drifting contacts with \(F_P(y)\in\{0,1\}\), while retaining the finite-sample band as a fallback outside regular strata? The required object must estimate the directional derivative rather than apply the ordinary bootstrap to the post-hinge endpoints, and it must characterize the local sequences on which exact coverage is attainable.
statements.justification: The open question isolates the genuinely nonregular inference problem instead of hiding it behind a smooth-stratum theorem.
statements.gap: Fang and Santos (2019) provide the general derivative-aware bootstrap and Masten, Poirier, and Zhang (2024) adapt it to sensitivity curves, but the local contact geometry of these propensity-mixture CDF endpoints has not been characterized.
statements.consumer: A positive answer would give shorter simultaneous bands for large-sample CDF and quantile analyses without sacrificing validity at empirically common atoms and active-face switches.

sampling_model.design: Observational sampling from a nonparametric bow-ADMG SCM in a fixed covariate stratum.
sampling_model.units: \((A_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^n\) are independent and identically distributed; potential outcomes and the latent confounder are unobserved.
sampling_model.overlap: Strict positivity \(0<e<1\) and mutual absolute continuity \(P\sim Q\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate \(e\) by the arm fraction and \(F_P\) by the empirical CDF within arm \(a\); the finite-sample band uses Hoeffding and conditional Dvoretzky--Kiefer--Wolfowitz radii.

estimand_functional: Without reverse support, \(\boldsymbol Q\in\mathfrak M^{\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)=\mathfrak L^{\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)=\mathfrak B^{\mathrm{ad},\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)\); under conditional reverse support, \(\boldsymbol Q\in\mathfrak M_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)=\mathfrak L_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)=\mathfrak B^{\mathrm{ad}}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)\), with all equalities on one common \(\mu_X\)-conull set. At a fixed stratum, \(Q_a=eP+(1-e)R\) with arbitrary \(R\) in the one-sided regime and \(R\ll P\) in the reverse-support regime; the corresponding CDF endpoint maps and simultaneous band retain their fixed-stratum scope.
target_estimand: \(\boldsymbol Q=(Q_0,Q_1),\quad Q_a(x,\cdot)=P(Y(a)\in\cdot\mid X=x)=P(Y\in\cdot\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a),X=x)\) as conditional-law versions defined on one common \(\mu_X\)-conull set

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Jung--Kang (2026) use Theorem 5 to calibrate the propensity-only divergence radius, define the resulting ambiguity class in equation (10), and optimize causal functionals over that class while presenting the framework as sharp partial identification with tight causal bounds. For every \(f\) outside the hinge class, the present open-illegality theorem proves that this divergence program contains a nonempty open set of full-support binary laws outside the bow-SCM feasible set; its extrema can therefore be exact for the declared divergence relaxation without being sharp for the bow-SCM model.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The unrestricted Huber contamination model \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\) yields the event-probability interval \([ep,ep+1-e]\). The present support split additionally proves the mutual-absolute-continuity boundary collapse at \(p=0,1\), atom-aware formulas, and endpoint attainment by bow-ADMG SCMs.
Its main theorem constructs density bands sharing least-favorable tests with divergence balls and its Discussion asks when the uncertainty sets themselves coincide.
Proposition 2.3 identifies Huber contamination with the forward linear-vacuous credal ball but does not supply the global conditional bow-SCM realization or generator frontier.
The paper develops functional domination and hinge tools for \(f\)-divergences under bounded relative information.
Theorem 2.1 reduces optimization under finitely many divergence constraints to small alphabets but does not prove the universal binary open-set dichotomy.
The paper certifies discrete causal bounds by response-function polynomial programs; it does not give analytic standard-Borel conditional realization or atom-aware fixed-stratum CDF endpoints.
The paper is an econometric precedent for repairing an over-wide sensitivity optimization by imposing the exact compatible weighting class.
The paper constructs confidence bands uniform over a scalar sensitivity index, not the piecewise fixed-stratum support-contact endpoint process here.
Directional-bootstrap methods apply on regular separated strata but cannot overcome total-variation indistinguishability across this note's discontinuous fixed-stratum support contacts.

tldr: The flagship result classifies exactly when the mutual-absolute-continuity version of the Jung--Kang \(f\)-divergence ambiguity class equals the compatible binary-treatment bow-SCM fiber for every law: modulo affine generator terms, \(f\) must vanish through the propensity cap and be strictly positive above it. Bow-mixture completeness, \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\) with \(R\ll P\), supplies the structural input, and a universal open illegal binary region supplies the stable converse, with explicit KL and hinge certificates. Exact atom-aware CDF endpoints, bounded-query support functions, simultaneous bands, and the \(\texttt{itbound}\) and IHDP legality correction are consequences and implementation layers.

project_justification.gap: Jung and Kang prove that every compatible interventional law belongs to a propensity-calibrated ambiguity class and optimize exactly over that class, yielding valid outer causal bounds; they do not establish that every ambiguity-class member is realizable by a bow SCM. Robust-statistics and information-theory papers separately provide contamination neighborhoods, hinge divergences, density bands, and finite-alphabet reductions, but none identifies all ordinary convex generators whose calibrated class exactly equals the bow-SCM law class or proves an open illegal region for every failure.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a generator-level causal legality frontier: a necessary-and-sufficient affine-invariant condition, with stable counterexamples when it fails and explicit causal endpoints when the exact cap is imposed.
project_justification.fill: The propensity-hinge iff is the sole flagship. Bow-SCM mixture completeness supplies its structural input, and the nondifferentiability-robust binary open-gap theorem supplies its stable converse, including explicit KL and hinge certificates. Sharp CDF and bounded-query formulas, distribution-free confidence bands, and the shared software cap are consequences and implementation layers.

related_work: Jung and Kang (2026, Assumption 4; Theorem 5, equations (3)--(4); proof in Appendix E) prove that every compatible interventional law lies in the propensity-calibrated \(f\)-divergence ambiguity class, and their later optimization is exact relative to that class. Those ambiguity-class extrema are valid outer causal bounds; the paper does not establish that every member is realizable by a bow SCM, whereas the flagship target characterizes exactly when the ambiguity class equals the compatible bow-SCM fiber. This proposal uses the mutual-absolute-continuity version under their Assumption 4: their equation (10) visibly states only \(P\ll Q\), while the maintained model and density parametrization supply \(Q\ll P\). Sason and Verdu (2016) supply affine normalization, bounded-relative-information, and \(E_\gamma\)-hinge machinery that motivates the cap-detecting direction. Guntuboyina, Saha, and Schiebinger (2014, Theorem 2.1 and Section 3) show why divergence geometry can be exposed on small alphabets, while the proposed necessity proof specializes the boundary analysis to a binary propensity cap. Fauss, Zoubir, and Poor (2018, main theorem and Discussion) equate least-favorable robust tests under divergence balls and constructed density bands and explicitly leave set equality and generator recovery open; the proposed iff resolves that question for the one-sided propensity band. Chen, Berrett, Damoulas, and Caprio (2026, Proposition 2.3) identify Huber contamination with a linear-vacuous credal ball, which establishes the noncausal mixture geometry but not the ordinary \(f\)-generator frontier or bow-SCM realization. Duarte et al. (2024) certify sharp causal bounds by response-function polynomial programs for discrete variables; the proposed latent construction is analytic and covers general standard Borel outcomes. Dorn and Guo (2023) provide the closest econometric precedent for repairing an over-wide sensitivity optimization by imposing the exact compatible weighting class. Masten, Poirier, and Zhang (2024) and Fang and Santos (2019) motivate the uniform and derivative-aware inference layer, respectively.
technical_internal_limitation: Pointwise attainment of \(L_e(F_P(y))\) and \(U_e(F_P(y))\) permits the attaining residual law to depend on \(y\). It does not imply that the entire lower or upper envelope is itself one counterfactual CDF. The complete process identified set remains \(\{eF_P+(1-e)F_R:R\ll P\}\), so any reported whole curve must retain a common residual CDF.
honest_scope: The mixture characterization and endpoint algebra have short candidate arguments, but every result remains \(\mathrm{to\text{-}prove}\) at this stage. The load-bearing open content is the fully quantified necessity and open-illegal-region dichotomy for finite continuous convex generators with kinks or extended zero faces. The finite-sample band is deliberately conservative at support contacts; asymptotically exact tie-adaptive inference is isolated as \(\mathrm{oeq:tie\text{-}adaptive\text{-}exact\text{-}band}\). The mixture and SCM classes and the endpoint maps alone extend to the boundary \(e=1\), where \(\mathfrak M_1(P)=\mathfrak L_1(P)=\{P\}\) and \(L_1(p)=U_1(p)=p\). No all-generator singleton claim is made for calibrated divergence classes at \(e=1\): a zero-radius \(f\)-class is a singleton only under an additional strict Jensen-equality or cap-detecting condition, and affine or identically zero generators are counterexamples. The flagship iff remains explicitly fixed at \(0<e<1\). The empirical IHDP deliverable is a reproducible before-and-after audit, not a theorem about the benchmark.
